status: UNSENT and UNADOPTED. Concrete reviewable proposed amendment only; no current rules/files modified.
scope: Explicitly extend only the current Mark Omen/Fate Coin common original-roll-lineage guard to Fate Reversal, subject to actual joint DE4 acceptance.
existingGuardVerbatim: Mark Omen and Fate Coin share one guard: an original roll event and its entire replacement lineage may receive at most one reroll from either of these two spells, across all casters, coins, marks and recasts. Reserve this allowance at the first legal activation's commitment, not after the replacement die resolves. For a multi-die roll, the whole set/pool is one original roll event; the resulting attack's separate later damage roll is a different event. A shared area-damage roll remains one event even when applied to several creatures. Other exact class reroll features keep their own permissions and timing, but do not erase this guard or create a fresh lineage for these two spells. If competing declarations are simultaneous, use current initiative order; outside initiative use a fixed neutral table order chosen before the roll. Only the first legal commitment spends a mark/coin; a later declaration barred by this guard spends nothing. No new Action, roll event, cast, payment or duplicated outcome hook is created by replacing dice.
proposedGuardVerbatim: NEW scoped DE4-GUARD-01 amendment: Mark Omen, Fate Coin and Fate Reversal share one guard: an original roll event and its entire replacement lineage may receive at most one reroll from any of these three spells, across all casters, coins, marks, Fate Reversal permissions and recasts. Reserve this allowance at the first legal activation's commitment, not after the replacement die resolves. For a multi-die roll, the whole set/pool is one original roll event; the resulting attack's separate later damage roll is a different event. A shared area-damage roll remains one event even when applied to several creatures. Other exact class reroll features keep their own permissions and timing, but do not erase this guard or create a fresh lineage for these three spells. If competing declarations are simultaneous, use current initiative order; outside initiative use a fixed neutral table order chosen before the roll. Only the first legal commitment spends its own actual mark, coin or Fate Reversal permission and any Reaction required by that source; a later declaration barred by this guard spends nothing. No new Action, roll event, cast, payment or duplicated outcome hook is created by replacing dice. This extension changes only the common lineage guard. Mark Omen still replaces the caster's own marked-target attack d20 procedure with no additional Action or Reaction; Fate Coin still changes exactly one eligible physical die through its holder's actual Reaction and30-foot perceived-event interface; Fate Reversal still requires its own Reaction, pending permission, eligible complete attack/save/check d20 procedure and60-foot perceived-event interface. No class feature is added to this family merely because it changes a roll, and this amendment grants no new access to hidden dice or any source's otherwise ineligible roll.

operations.before: Ordinary shapechange retaining creature identity does not remove the mark. Actual death, destruction or ended summoned existence ends it; revival/reconstruction/resummoning does not revive that application. Information-only protection does not itself cancel this noninformational reroll permission. No ammo, RP, component, class use or other original attack cost is refunded or charged again, and the replaced result produces no separate hit/miss/on-hit outcome. A legally committed mark stays spent if an exact later interrupt prevents completion. Other exact class reroll features keep their own permissions and timing, but do not erase this guard or create a fresh lineage for these two spells. If competing declarations are simultaneous, use current initiative order; outside initiative use a fixed neutral table order chosen before the roll. Only the first legal commitment spends a mark/coin; a later declaration barred by this guard spends nothing. No new Action, roll event, cast, payment or duplicated outcome hook is created by replacing dice. A successful replacement owns its new endpoint; stale cleanup cannot remove it. A failed or countered cast creates no replacement, although an applicable concentration transition has already happened. Actual class access, repertoire, V/S/F components, costs, Dissonance/Refrain, beginning hooks, concentration transitions and interruption follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Costs commit before the counter window without refunds or restoration of prior concentration. Explicit remote-destination/concealment exceptions override ordinary originating line of effect only as printed. Specific information protections apply to their actual subject and generating-source scope; hidden but unprotected facts are valid information, and missing facts are never invented. No automatic scaling or upcast.

operations.before: One active Fate Coin per caster; successful recasting replaces the previous unspent coin wherever it is. Ordinary handing/dropping/custody and hands apply; a handoff never refreshes the charge, endpoint or caster cap. requiredFocusedExamples: Mark Omen reserves the lineage for an advantage attack; later legal-looking Fate Reversal is barred with no permission/Reaction spend.
Fate Reversal reserves an eligible complete save/check d20 lineage; later Coin cannot reroll one of its replacement dice.
